analyst_followup.basis: Manual analyst enrichment from public sources beyond the Companies House filing. The machine-generated brief above is unchanged.
findings: Product (verified on vectisbiosciences.com, 21 Jul 2026): a live tool for mechanistic drug-safety prediction from molecular structure, aimed at novel drug classes (PROTAC, CELMoD, IMiD) that lack clinical safety history. Pipeline: molecular docking (AutoDock Vina, 143 protein structures) -> signalling-cascade modelling (OmniPath, 1,516 genes) -> GNN refinement (LINCS-trained) -> adverse-event classification (21 FDA-label-trained classifiers). Claims external validation of Spearman R=0.77 (p=0.005) against independent RNA-seq on held-out drugs (e.g. lenalidomide, imatinib), across 22 drugs and 8 mechanism classes.

Founder (per director LinkedIn, to confirm on a call): Alice Condrat is an Oxford biochemistry graduate with a drug-discovery background and stated ties to the University pharmacology department and an established lab -- directly relevant domain expertise.

Spinout status (speculative, not established): references to Oxford-based advisors and possible Oxford Science Enterprises involvement would make this a bona-fide university spinout. Unconfirmed -- a key question for a first call.
